title: Kyi waing
summary: The kyi waing is a ring of kettle gongs, often twenty or more, hung on cords inside a low carved circular frame. A single player sits in the middle and plays quick, glittering tunes with two small beaters.
howToPlay: A ring of gongs is lit; the lowest sits at the front left and the pitch climbs round the circle.
Strike each gong as its ring closes. The beater visits it and the bronze answers.
Runs go round the circle, so keep your eyes moving.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The gong circle is tuned note by note, small gongs for the high notes and larger ones for the low. Its frame is lacquered red and gilded.
credits: Tradition: the kyi waing of Myanmar; patterns written for this game
